moves.pick: one person took the horse and killed the trainer who got in the way

moves.pick: a drug for the boy's supper

moves.pick: to see that all was well with the horses

moves.pick: to see that all was well with the horses
moves.why: He took a surgeon's blade and a candle and was found a quarter-mile out on the moor. That is not a check on the stables.

moves.pick: a friend of Straker's, as Mrs. Straker says

moves.pick: a friend of Straker's, as Mrs. Straker says
moves.why: The friend's bill was in Straker's pocket, his letters come to Straker's house, and Mrs. Straker never had such a dress.

This is only what Straker told his wife. The bill and the letters point to Straker himself.

moves.pick: a woman Straker kept without his wife's knowledge
moves.why: The bill was in Straker's pocket, yet his wife never had such a dress. The clothes went to another woman.

There was no wind and the coat was laid across the bush, calmly, not torn off.

moves.pick: he took it off for some task
moves.why: In heavy rain he took his coat off and laid it on the bush. He needed his arms free for something.
Straker carried a box of vestas and a candle. The match in the hollow is most likely his.

moves.pick: by habit, or to light his pipe
moves.why: Holmes went looking for a burnt match in the hollow and found one. A light was used down there.

moves.pick: to have a small light somewhere out on the moor
moves.why: He carried a candle and matches, and a match was struck in the hollow, out of sight of the stable.

moves.for: hyp:q.candle=to have a small light somewhere out on the moor
moves.why: The match he struck in the hollow is the light he took the candle and vestas for.

moves.of: hyp:q.candle=to have a small light somewhere out on the moor

moves.pick: one person took the horse and killed the trainer who got in the way

moves.pick: he meant to return the horse, then decided to keep it
moves.why: He set off towards the horse's own stable, then came back and took it in at Mapleton, whose horse is second favourite.

moves.why: To keep the favourite out of the race, what would he have to do with it?

moves.pick: he found the horse loose and took it in
moves.why: The horse came alone, a man met it near Mapleton and took it in, and Brown is first up there.

The track led to Mapleton, Brown is broken, and Holmes told Ross to keep the horse entered.

moves.pick: at the race for the Wessex Cup on Tuesday

moves.pick: yes: he will be found fit and run on Tuesday

moves.pick: put its appearance back as it was, after it had been altered

moves.pick: to do something to the horse himself

moves.pick: to make some fine cut on the horse
moves.why: A blade for very delicate cuts, uncorked by himself, beside the horse, after sheep were lamed.

moves.pick: nobody meant to carry him off: he was led out to be harmed and got loose

moves.pick: to do something to him that could not be done in the stall
